title: Lalita's two addresses
hook: goddesses of speech compose a thousand names, and two of them are addresses
carry: one goddess, on the altar and within
tomorrow: the sleeper wakes at the bottom of the road. where is she going?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the chakras as a map reached the heart: anahata, the sound heard within that nothing strikes, beside Elijah's still small voice. Today, the whole week meets in one Goddess.

In the Brahmanda Purana, the sage Agastya studies with Hayagriva, the horse-headed form of Vishnu, and hears the story of the Goddess Lalita. One thing his teacher holds back: her thousand names. When Agastya finally asks, Hayagriva tells him where they came from. The Goddess herself commanded the goddesses of speech to compose them, and they sang the names before her whole court. That's the Lalita Sahasranama, still chanted in homes and temples. And tucked among the thousand names are two addresses.
screen: `A TEACHER HOLDS ONE THING BACK.` → `THE GODDESSES OF SPEECH COMPOSE IT.` → `A THOUSAND NAMES, TWO ADDRESSES.`

segments.voice: Near the end, she's Sri Chakra Raja Nilaya: she whose home is the Sri Chakra, the king of chakras. That's the Sri Yantra, this week's first map, which is also called the Sri Chakra. Chakra: a wheel, a circle. And early in the list, another run of names places her in the body: she who dwells in the Muladhara, the root, and, simply, Kundalini. Same Goddess. Two addresses. This is the Shakta teaching the week has been climbing toward: the Goddess worshipped on the altar's diagram is the same power coiled at the base of every person. That's why one word, chakra, names both maps. Look back and the week falls into place. Pusalar's temple in the mind, and the Bhavana Upanishad: the worshipper is the map. Jagannath's unfinished wood: the presence is invited, not bought. Bhrigu's layers: more of you than flesh. Kundalini asleep at the root. Indra at the water: the atman isn't the body in the mirror. And at the heart, a sound nothing strikes. So when someone asks why a Hindu grandmother bows to a brass diagram and also sits in silence with her eyes closed, it's one worship. She's visiting the same Goddess at both addresses.
screen: `HER HOME: THE SRI CHAKRA.` · `HER HOME: THE ROOT, AS KUNDALINI.` · `ONE GODDESS, TWO ADDRESSES.` · `THE WEEK, BACK FOR ONE PASS.` · then, large: `ON THE ALTAR AND WITHIN.`

segments.voice: If you pray, say three of the Goddess's names slowly, with a breath between: Lalita. Sri Chakra Raja Nilaya. Kundalini. Feel where each one lands, out on the altar or here within. If you don't pray, say the week's lines instead, worship in the mind is real, invited not bought, more than flesh, and sit with the one that stayed.
The chakras as a map: wheels, circles, centers. One word names the body's lotuses and the Sri Chakra, and one Goddess lives in both.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Last line of the week: one Goddess, on the altar and within. Two addresses, one road.

howItsDone: The Lalita Sahasranama, the thousand names of the Goddess Lalita, is chanted in homes and temples, especially in Sri Vidya, where the Sri Yantra is also called the Sri Chakra; the chakras of the body are approached in meditation, usually with a teacher.

fork.reveal: the Lalita Sahasranama names her home as the Sri Chakra, and also names her Kundalini, dwelling at the root. chakra, a wheel, names both maps.
